rationale: SWIFTD21, the ontology lane DERIV_EXPORTS_SWIFT3. `@_exported import M` is the only Swift construct that says "this file's module re-publishes M". Measured before the fix: 0 `exports` edges on any corpus, against 40 `@_exported import` sites in 27 files of swift-corpus (script/m14/swift-ontology-census.ts probe P2, instrument B). Line pins were read off the source with `nl -ba` and cross-checked against the module-name node's own startPosition, so they are checkable rather than inherited from the declaration. The attribute sits on its own line (10) and the module name on 11 so that an edge lined at the DECLARATION's start is distinguishable from one lined at the module name's own site. SUPERSESSION (M14 swift lane, 2026-10-23) — SOURCE SPELLING PLUS ONE ROW THAT THE LATER RULING REVERSED. (1) The exports SOURCE was pinned `root`; the standing ruling DERIV_EXPORTS_SWIFT4 makes it the FILE'S LEAF NAME, and the SAME-CORPUS PASSING fixture swift/exports-visibility pins that in both directions (EXPECTS `exports exports-visibility -> Shape`; FORBIDS `exports root -> Shape`, because `root` is in parallel-indexer's SYMBOL_NAME_DENYLIST and an edge sourced there can never bind). (2) The forbid `exports root -> Holder` is SUPERSEDED and flipped into an EXPECT. Its old rationale — 'a `public struct` is part of the module interface, but a Swift FILE declares no module, so there is no file-level construct to source the edge from' — is precisely the argument DERIV_EXPORTS_SWIFT4 overruled: the leaf name is a name for the FILE, not a claim about SwiftPM's module, and exports-visibility EXPECTS the identical shape for its own public top-level declarations. Keeping a forbid against a claim the ruling requires would make this fixture contradict a passing peer. The flip does not weaken coverage: the positive pin is strictly stronger than a forbid on a spelling nothing emits. (3) Every REMAINING forbid is re-sourced to the leaf name, because a forbid against `root` would now be VACUOUS — no such edge exists, and an assertion that cannot fire asserts nothing. A generic forbid on ANY root-sourced `exports` edge is ADDED. The two module re-export rows keep their targets and line pins (11, 14) and gain the ruled vocabulary (`exportForm`, `reExport`, `evidenceClass`). Predecessor kept byte-identical as reexported-import.expectation.superseded-1c303e66768215ad.json (`sha256 1c303e66768215a…`); the byte-identical corpus-import twin reexported-import.expectation.superseded-e7c9819f4.json is left in place. The corrected rows are derived from the ruling and this fixture's source; the analyzer output was read only to CHARACTERIZE the defect.

RULING: a plain `import` is not a re-export. This is the assertion the SWIFTD21 probe turns on — a mutant that made every import an export dies here. Re-sourced so it can fire.

RULING: `@testable` is a READ-widening attribute. Publishing it as an export would be a fabricated edge: the file's module does not re-publish the tested module, it reads it. Re-sourced so it can fire.

RULING, second half: a `public var` member rides `contains` (family contract, go GO7 and the JVM-closure export-uniqueness invariant), so it is not a second publication edge. Re-sourced so it can fire.
